clinician.trajectory_summary: A 71-year-old male presented on 11/03/2021 with palpitations, leg cramps, fatigue, dizziness, and loss of balance. Orthostatic hypotension was ruled out. Initial medication included amlodipine, aspirin, atorvastatin, lisinopril, and prednisone. Coronary angiography and vertebral artery imaging performed revealed moderate LAD artery disease, left vertebral artery occlusion at the ostium, and severe (80-90%) stenosis of the proximal right vertebral artery with preserved ejection fraction of 55-60%. MRI brain showed generalized cerebral atrophy without acute ischemic or hemorrhagic events. Follow-up documented worsening dizziness, fatigue, and balance issues. No physical or neurological exam details were reported.
